applies_to: WGS, whole genome, human
basis: Review states the expected Ti/Tv ratio is around 2.0 across the whole genome, and 2.1 is the often-cited point estimate.

applies_to: coding regions only (WES, or the exonic subset of a WGS callset)
basis: Review states that in coding regions the Ti/Tv ratio is generally reported to be between 3 and 4. Present so a genome-wide value is never compared against an exome expectation.

applies_to: WGS, EUR-like genetic ancestry
basis: Review states the expected Het/Hom ratio is around 1.5-1.6 for EUR-like populations.

applies_to: WGS, AFR-like genetic ancestry
basis: Review states that for AFR-like populations it is approximately 1.9-2.0.

applies_to: WGS, AMR-like genetic ancestry
basis: Review reports a higher variability from 1.3 to 1.7 for AMR-like populations.

applies_to: one genome vs GRCh37/GRCh38 reference
source: 1000 Genomes Project Consortium (Auton) 2015, Nature, PMID 26432245, DOI 10.1038/nature15393
basis: Paper states a typical genome differs from the reference human genome at 4.1 million to 5.0 million sites.

applies_to: median autosomal SNP sites per genome, range across the five 1000G superpopulations
source: 1000 Genomes Project Consortium (Auton) 2015, Nature, PMID 26432245, DOI 10.1038/nature15393
basis: Table 1 median autosomal SNP sites per genome: EUR 3.53M and EAS 3.55M at the low end, AFR 4.31M at the high end.

applies_to: median autosomal indel sites per genome, range across the five 1000G superpopulations
source: 1000 Genomes Project Consortium (Auton) 2015, Nature, PMID 26432245, DOI 10.1038/nature15393
basis: Table 1 median autosomal indel sites per genome: EAS and EUR 546k at the low end, AFR 625k at the high end.

applies_to: one genome, SV callers only (not in a short-variant VCF)
source: 1000 Genomes Project Consortium (Auton) 2015, Nature, PMID 26432245, DOI 10.1038/nature15393
basis: Paper states the typical genome contains an estimated 2,100 to 2,500 structural variants affecting about 20 million bases.

applies_to: one genome, WGS, GRCh38, small variants, vs dbSNP build 149; point estimate not a range
basis: Paper states: We identified an average of 3.78 million variants in each genome. Among these, an average of 30,207 (0.8%) were novel and 3,510 (0.1%) were singletons. Table footnote defines novel as not present in dbSNP build 149, the most recent dbSNP version without TOPMed submissions. Membership = 100 - 0.8. Against a post-TOPMed dbSNP build the rate can only be higher.

applies_to: WGS, SNP concordance with an external database, spread across published studies
basis: Review states SNP concordance values vary substantially between publications and range from approximately 70% to almost 100%. WIDE BY THE SOURCE'S OWN ADMISSION - kept only to show how much published practice varies; grade a callset against the Taliun per-genome row instead.

applies_to: one genome, WGS 30x, GRCh38, unfiltered short-variant callset; range across the five 1000G superpopulations
basis: DERIVED, not quoted: Table 1 per-sample average insertions divided by deletions. AFR 465797/503995 = 0.9242 (low), EAS and SAS 0.9364 (high), cohort-wide 420646/451277 = 0.9321. Deletions consistently exceed insertions.

applies_to: one genome, WGS 30x, GRCh38; range across the five 1000G superpopulations
basis: Table 1 per-sample average SNVs: EUR 3,818,951 at the low end, AFR 4,653,521 at the high end, cohort-wide 4,080,992. Prefer this over the phase-3 row when comparing a high-coverage callset - phase 3 was low-coverage and undercounts.

applies_to: one genome, WGS 30x, GRCh38, insertions plus deletions; range across the five 1000G superpopulations
basis: DERIVED: Table 1 per-sample insertions + deletions. EUR 399,298 + 426,940 = 826,238 (low), AFR 465,797 + 503,995 = 969,792 (high), cohort-wide 871,923.

applies_to: one trio, genome-wide, point estimate not a range
source: Pedersen 2021, npj Genomic Medicine, PMID 34267211, DOI 10.1038/s41525-021-00227-3
basis: Paper states an average of about 70 de novo SNV and INDEL mutations should be observed genome-wide. Point estimate reported as such - low and high are equal on purpose.

applies_to: WGS, median project coverage, point estimate not a range
basis: Review describes median coverage around 35x in many current projects. Point estimate reported as such.

applies_to: gnomAD population AF filter for recessive and compound-heterozygous models
source: Pedersen 2021, npj Genomic Medicine, PMID 34267211, DOI 10.1038/s41525-021-00227-3
basis: Methods require a frequency below 0.01 for recessive and compound-heterozygous inheritance models. Corroborated by Whiffin 2017 PMID 28518168, which names 1% as the value often invoked as a conservative frequency cutoff for recessive disease.

applies_to: gnomAD population AF filter for de novo and autosomal dominant models
source: Pedersen 2021, npj Genomic Medicine, PMID 34267211, DOI 10.1038/s41525-021-00227-3
basis: Methods require AF below 0.001 in each of the eight gnomAD populations under de novo and autosomal dominant models. Corroborated by Whiffin 2017 PMID 28518168, which names 0.1% as the cutoff often invoked for dominant disease.

applies_to: one trio, WGS, after AF + GQ + AB filtering, all inheritance models
source: Pedersen 2021, npj Genomic Medicine, PMID 34267211, DOI 10.1038/s41525-021-00227-3
basis: Whole-genome cohort of 94 trios yields a mean of 13.1 candidate variants with DeepVariant and 18.3 with GATK.

applies_to: one trio, WGS, after filtering, compound-heterozygous model only, point estimate
source: Pedersen 2021, npj Genomic Medicine, PMID 34267211, DOI 10.1038/s41525-021-00227-3
basis: Of the mean 13.1 candidates per whole-genome trio, 9.2 are compound heterozygotes. Point estimate reported as such.
